title: LLM moderation failures are returned as requiring manual review but do not set the review flag
reasoning: When LLM moderation raises, the task returns requires_manual_review=True and sends the manual-review email, but it only writes moderation_result before saving. It does not set requires_human_review=True, moderated_at, or any severity/status marker. The admin is explicitly built around requires_human_review filters and list display, so failed moderation requests can be omitted from the primary manual-review queue despite the task reporting that manual review is required.
reproduction: Cause Anthropic JSON parsing or API access to fail for a pending request. After the task returns {'requires_manual_review': True}, inspect the PrayerRequest: requires_human_review remains its default False, so filtering the admin by Requires human review misses it.
recommendation: In the LLM error branch, set requires_human_review=True, keep status as pending_moderation, set moderated_at if appropriate, and consider a moderation_severity value or explicit error marker that makes the admin queue visible and sortable.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise moderation task failure paths or assert admin/manual-review visibility after an LLM exception.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock Anthropic to raise or return invalid JSON, run moderate_prayer_request_task, and assert the request remains pending_moderation with requires_human_review=True and the saved moderation_result contains the error.
minimumFixScope: LLM exception branch in prayers/tasks.py plus a focused task test.
